paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using CoT and . The results indicate that while easier problems are mainly hindered by a lack of knowledge, the bottleneck for hard problems lies in geometric knowledge reasoning abilities.
model_annotation: The image presents three pie charts displaying the distribution of problems based on correctness under different settings, specifically with and without knowledge. Each chart represents a distinct level of difficulty: easy, medium, and hard. The charts are divided into four categories, represented by different colors, as indicated by the legend: N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (yellow), N-K- (orange), and N+K- (red). The easy chart consists of four slices, with N-K+ at 45.9%, N+K+ at 40.6%, N-K- at 10.1%, and N+K- at 3.3%. The medium chart also has four slices, with N-K+ at 44.3%, N+K+ at 44.6%, N-K- at 7.2%, and N+K- at 3.9%. The hard chart comprises four slices as well, with N-K- at 36.8%, N+K+ at 36.2%, N-K+ at 20.1%, and N+K- at 7.0%. A legend is provided to the right of the charts, and percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The segments within each chart appear to be arranged in descending order of size.
